title: TNS Media Intelligence Releases March Madness Advertising Trends Report – Sports Video Group

facts.fact: According to TNS Media Intelligence, over $2.73 billion has been spent on network TV advertising during NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament games from 2000-2006.
facts.quote:
over  
 $2.73 billion has been spent on network TV advertising during the tournament games from 2000-2006

facts.fact: TNS Media Intelligence expected 2007 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament ad spending to surpass $500 million, an all-time high.
facts.quote: For 2007, ad spending is expected to surpass $500 million in 2007 an all-time high

facts.fact: TNS Media Intelligence projected a 65 to 70 percent increase in NCAA Tournament ad spending in the current decade.
facts.quote: a 65 to 70 percent increase in the current decade

facts.fact: On average, 83 percent of the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament's network TV ad revenue comes from returning advertisers.
facts.quote: On average, 83 percent of the Tournament s network TV ad revenue comes from returning advertisers.

facts.fact: The top 10 advertisers in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament spent almost $1.1 billion over the past seven years.
facts.quote: the top 10 advertisers in the Tournament have spent almost $1.1 billion to promote their brands in the games

facts.fact: The top 10 advertisers' spending accounted for about 40 percent of total network TV ad revenue generated by the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament.
facts.quote:
accounting for about  
 40 percent of total network TV ad revenue generated by the event.

facts.fact: Nearly 75 percent of measured national TV advertising dollars spent in college basketball each year are spent in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament.
facts.quote:
Nearly  
 75 percent of all measured national TV advertising dollars that are spent in college basketball each year are spent in the Tournament.

facts.fact: Regular season college basketball games account for the remaining 25 percent of measured national TV ad dollars, with over 300 nationally televised men's basketball games each season.
facts.quote: Regular season games account for the remaining 25 percent – and there are over 300 nationally televised men s basketball games each season

facts.fact: College and professional football TV ad revenue is distributed with 75 to 80 percent from the regular season and 20 to 25 percent from the post-season.
facts.quote: college and professional football TV ad revenue is distributed exactly the opposite with 75 to 80 percent coming from the regular season

facts.fact: For the 2006 Tournament, CBS signed up 18 advertisers to sponsor NCAA March Madness on Demand webcasts.
facts.quote: For the 2006 Tournament, CBS signed up 18 advertisers to sponsor these webcasts

facts.fact: In 2007, CBS offered all games from the first three rounds of the Tournament streamed live online at no charge to PC users with a broadband connection.
facts.quote: All games from the first three rounds of the Tournament will be streamed live over the internet, available at no charge to PC users with a broadband connection.

facts.fact: Cingular ran a sweepstakes offering a chance to step onto the court and make a basket for $5 million during the 2006 Tournament.
facts.quote: a chance to step onto the court and make a basket for $5 million.

facts.fact: The NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament began March 13 (2007 season), per the article.
facts.quote: the NCAA Men s Basketball Tournament beginning March 13th

facts.fact: A Sports Video Group headline reports that the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams in 2027.
facts.quote: The College Football Playoff Will Expand to 24 Teams in 2027; ESPN Secures Rights to 12 Additional Games
